source_text:
## Acceptance checklist (2026-09-30)

- [ ] The improved pipeline completes on an all-arXiv-math corpus of at least 200,000 papers.
- [ ] Stage 9b reports pairwise cosine-similarity standard deviation above 0.10 and validation accuracy below 90%.
- [ ] A learn-to-swim or LeanDojo pilot record shows structural or hybrid retrieval finds technique-relevant papers missed by BGE-only retrieval.
- [ ] `corpus_ws_bridge.py` serves a FAISS index whose measured retrieval precision exceeds the BGE-only Mark 1 baseline.

| Mission | Relationship |
|---------|-------------|
| M-apm-solutions | Consumer: uses retrieval for theorem proving |
| M-diagramprover | Shares superpod, separate workflow (proof search not mining) |
| M-artificial-stack-exchange | Future consumer of improved retrieval |
| M-distributed-frontiermath | Future consumer for FrontierMath campaigns |

fragments.rationale: The heading declares that what follows is a dated list of conditions for calling the mission done, written before any of them is met; nothing below is a status report.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern asks for the bar to be fixed in advance so it cannot be moved to fit what was produced. A dated checklist of numeric and comparative conditions is that kind of advance statement, though this mission doc does not say the list is sealed or protected from later edits.

pattern_rejections.reason: Its move is to turn prose bands into a runnable checker run by someone other than the producer. The heading only frames the list; the items below are still prose checkboxes, so that pattern names a next step for them, not what this fragment does.
pattern_rejections.query: numeric quality gate encoded as a checkable threshold

pattern_rejections.reason: It warns about a done bit that closes over an unfinished artifact. The '[ ]' boxes are binary, but this heading only announces the list; the risk applies to how the boxes get ticked later.
pattern_rejections.query: acceptance criteria stated as checkable conditions before the work counts as done

fragments.rationale: The first condition is that the whole improved pipeline runs to the end; no quality figure is attached to this item, the later items supply those.

pattern_rejections.reason: A bare 'completes' is the kind of binary status the pattern says can be true while the output is unusable. Items 2 to 4 add artifact-level figures, so this fragment is not itself a fake-done instance; it is the part that would be if it stood alone.
pattern_rejections.query: acceptance criteria stated as checkable conditions before the work counts as done

fragments.text: on an all-arXiv-math corpus of at least 200,000 papers
fragments.target: the corpus the pipeline must complete on
fragments.rationale: Fixes the scale at which completion counts: the whole arXiv math corpus, at least 200,000 papers, not a sample.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern says that once a run is fast and checkpointed, point it at the whole corpus instead of a capped subset and gate the first checkpoint. This item asks for exactly the whole-corpus run; the source does not mention checkpointing or an early gate.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern is about a small held-out real-backend pass before the paid run. This fragment states the end-state scale of the run, not a pre-run sample.
pattern_rejections.query: run the full pipeline at corpus scale before declaring it works

fragments.text: Stage 9b reports pairwise cosine-similarity standard deviation above 0.10
fragments.target: the spread of pairwise cosine similarities reported by stage 9b
fragments.rationale: A lower bound on how spread out the vectors are, as a number the stage itself reports; a value under 0.10 fails the item.

pattern_refs.rationale: A band with a stated number that the pipeline prints and a checker can compare is what the pattern asks for in place of a prose judgement. Here the stage reports the figure and the checklist fixes the threshold.

pattern_rejections.reason: About keeping a patterns-index and compression log so the sigil-based 'fake embedding' in FUTON3 stays reproducible. It does not concern a threshold on the spread of learned vectors; the hit was on the word 'embedding'.
pattern_rejections.query: embedding similarity spread as a collapse check on learned vectors

fragments.target: the validation accuracy reported by stage 9b
fragments.rationale: A ceiling, not a floor: validation accuracy has to stay under 90%. The doc does not say why; read literally, the item fails a run whose validation task is too easy or saturated.

pattern_refs.rationale: Same gate shape as the previous fragment: a numeric band with a pass or fail. The direction is unusual (fail if too high), and the source gives no reason for it.

pattern_rejections.reason: It says to probe the promised property instead of a cheap proxy. Accuracy under 90% could be read as a guard against a proxy, but the source does not say so, and the fragment states a threshold rather than a probe design.
pattern_rejections.query: validation accuracy too high means the test is too easy

fragments.text: A learn-to-swim or LeanDojo pilot record shows
fragments.target: a recorded pilot on learn-to-swim or LeanDojo material
fragments.rationale: The evidence has to be a pilot record on one of two named tasks; a claim of improvement without the record does not satisfy the item.

pattern_rejections.reason: 'Pilot' there is a role in a two-agent split (one flies the peripheral, one repairs the instrument). Here it is a small trial run whose record serves as evidence; the hit was on the word.
pattern_rejections.query: a pilot record is the evidence that a method works before scaling

fragments.text: structural or hybrid retrieval finds technique-relevant papers missed by BGE-only retrieval
fragments.target: structural or hybrid retrieval versus BGE-only retrieval
fragments.rationale: The claim to be shown is a difference in what is found: papers relevant to a technique that the embedding-only baseline misses, not a general score gain.

pattern_rejections.reason: It sets up A/B comparison with rotated seeds and repeated batches so variance can be estimated. This item asks only that a pilot record show the difference; it does not require repeats or variance estimates.
pattern_rejections.query: retrieval precision measured against a fixed earlier baseline

fragments.rationale: Names the concrete deliverable: the bridge script must actually serve a FAISS index, so a script that exists but serves nothing does not count.

pattern_rejections.reason: About binding subjects to warrants and closing incidents only with fresher ones. The fragment names a service that must be running, not a warrant or incident.
pattern_rejections.query: service must serve an index whose quality is measured, not asserted

fragments.text: whose measured retrieval precision exceeds the BGE-only Mark 1 baseline
fragments.target: retrieval precision of the served index against the Mark 1 baseline
fragments.rationale: The item passes only if a measured precision figure for the served index is above the figure for the earlier BGE-only Mark 1 system, so two numbers have to exist and be comparable.

pattern_refs.rationale: The item depends on two computed precision numbers being compared. The pattern says each such number should carry its rule and inputs so a dispute can be settled by checking; without that, 'exceeds the baseline' cannot be checked by someone other than whoever ran it. The source does not require this, so the pattern names a gap, not something the item already does.

pattern_rejections.reason: It derives an accepted Lean baseline from the distribution over a whole corpus. 'Baseline' here is the earlier system's measured precision, not a distribution-derived acceptance rule.
pattern_rejections.query: retrieval precision measured against a fixed earlier baseline

fragments.rationale: The header says each row below pairs a mission with how it relates to M-superpod-mark2.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern asks for missions to be linked by typed relationships (blocks, enables, shares, parent-child) so dependencies are visible; this table is the doc's version, with free-text relationship cells.

sentences.unresolved_reason: Markdown table separator row (dashes and pipes). It carries no words and no content of its own.

fragments.text: | M-apm-solutions | Consumer: uses retrieval for theorem proving |
fragments.target: M-apm-solutions and its relationship to M-superpod-mark2
fragments.rationale: M-apm-solutions is downstream of this mission: it uses the retrieval for theorem proving, so it is affected by whether the retrieval improves.

pattern_refs.rationale: Downstream consumer relationship, close to the pattern's 'enables' type, recorded from the enabling mission's side.

pattern_rejections.reason: About one provenance classifier serving several consumers instead of per-consumer filters. The word 'consumer' matches; the fragment declares a mission relationship, not a shared classifier.
pattern_rejections.query: table of missions and how each relates: consumer, shares resource, future consumer

fragments.text: | M-diagramprover | Shares superpod, separate workflow (proof search not mining) |
fragments.target: M-diagramprover and its relationship to M-superpod-mark2
fragments.rationale: M-diagramprover uses the same superpod but does a different job (proof search, not mining), so it competes for the machine without depending on this mission's output.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern's 'shares' type: two missions share a resource, and the parenthesis states that the work itself is separate.

fragments.text: | M-artificial-stack-exchange | Future consumer of improved retrieval |
fragments.target: M-artificial-stack-exchange and its relationship to M-superpod-mark2
fragments.rationale: M-artificial-stack-exchange is expected to use the improved retrieval later; nothing is blocked now, but its needs are a reason to finish.

pattern_refs.rationale: A soft, later downstream relationship, like 'enables' with the timing marked as future.

pattern_rejections.reason: It scans devmaps for declared prerequisites and reports what blocks what. This row declares a future consumer and states no blocker or unmet prerequisite.
pattern_rejections.query: state the relationship between missions so blocked and shared work is visible

fragments.text: | M-distributed-frontiermath | Future consumer for FrontierMath campaigns |
fragments.target: M-distributed-frontiermath and its relationship to M-superpod-mark2
fragments.rationale: M-distributed-frontiermath is expected to use the retrieval later, for FrontierMath campaigns.

pattern_refs.rationale: Same relationship as the row above, with the intended use named.
